header.name: Introduction to Bioenergetics
header.description: This course is designed to prepare the fundamental concepts of bioenergetics, which are prerequisites for understanding metabolism. It will introduce students to the energy transformation in biological systems, understanding coupled biochemical processes, and the crucial role of electrons, ions, and light in many biological events. Moreover, the students will be acquainted with the methods for probing the energetics of those events, which will broaden their scope of exploration of biological systems in the future.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will get an idea of looking at the biological processes through a thermodynamic perspective, and develop a foundation of bioenergetics

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be introduced to energetics of ions or more specifically electron flows in biological systems, and the energetics associated with it.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will get a brief overview of photochemistry and a detailed understanding of energy transformations during light-driven electron flow in photosynthesis

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Finally, students will be briefly introduced to a few crucial physical methods to probe the energy transformation in biological events.

lecture_topics: Revisiting chemical thermodynamics to understand biological energy transformation
Energetics of biological reactions, including redox couples
Ion transport across membranes, transport pathways
Energetics for ion transport across membranes
photochemistry and time scales for light-driven biochemical reactions
